hook: Robin Rombach is the lead author of the Latent Diffusion Models paper produced with the CompVis group at LMU Munich, the research that became the technical basis for Stable Diffusion. After a physics degree at Heidelberg and a PhD at LMU Munich, he continued the work as Research Director at Stability AI before leaving in 2024. In August 2024 he co-founded Black Forest Labs with two of his Latent Diffusion co-authors, Patrick Esser and Andreas Blattmann, releasing the FLUX.1 image model on launch day. He now runs Black Forest Labs as CEO from labs in Freiburg and San Francisco, and in 2026 spoke at the G7 alongside heads of state to argue for keeping frontier visual AI development open.

standing.record: The site's records on Rombach run along two lines, his research lineage and his time at Stability AI. The only company it holds for him is Stability AI, a London startup founded in 2019, where he is recorded as an executive. Its litigation record consists of five matters naming Stability AI entities: EVOX Productions LLC v. Stability AI, Inc., Anders v. Stability AI US Services Corporation, Getty Images (US), Inc. v. Stability AI, Ltd., Getty Images (US), Inc. v. Stability AI, Inc., and Andersen v. Stability AI Ltd. None of these cases names him personally, and the coverage the site holds ties him to the G7 appearance and to the Latent Diffusion paper rather than to the courtroom. The pattern is that his documented legal footprint here passes through Stability AI, while Black Forest Labs appears in his profile and quick facts but not in the company records.
standing.standing: Robin Rombach is co-founder and CEO of Black Forest Labs, the company he started on August 1, 2024 with fellow Latent Diffusion co-authors Patrick Esser and Andreas Blattmann, which builds the FLUX image and video generation models and raised 31 million dollars in seed funding led by Andreessen Horowitz. He is the first author of 'High-Resolution Image Synthesis with Latent Diffusion Models' (2021), the paper underlying Stable Diffusion, written with Blattmann, Dominik Lorenz, Esser and Bjorn Ommer. He studied physics at the University of Heidelberg and pursued his PhD at LMU Munich in the CompVis group, then served as Research Director at Stability AI before leaving in 2024, and the site lists Stability AI as a company where he is an executive. In 2026 he spoke at the G7 summit to advocate for open innovation in visual AI, appearing alongside heads of state including President Macron and President Trump. He runs Black Forest Labs from labs in Freiburg and San Francisco.
